critic.verdict: Publish. The pull-back clearly serves the loss in the story: it opens tight on the official bending over the fallen lifter, then visibly widens to the final full-hall dwell frame revealing the dropped barbell, silent paper crowd and hard overhead lights. Both first and last frames are strong still pictures that work in either direction, the light-sweep is subtle, and the 1950s offset-lithograph style is preserved. The plate itself has no stray text, no drawn faces where silhouettes/from-behind figures were directed, no anachronism, and no mangled anatomy or objects.

rounds.verdict: Do not publish: the story idea is present, but the visual movement is too timid and the opening barbell clipping is a clear composition fault.
filmIssues: The pull-back idea is right for a loss of consciousness, but the move is modest and reads largely as a slight widening and rightward settling rather than a clear dramatic reveal.

At t=0 the zoomed, off-centre framing awkwardly clips the dropped barbell at the left frame edge; it remains clipped through the early frames, weakening both the opening picture and the supposed reveal.

The official is a separate layer while the fallen lifter remains in the background, yet the official drifts down and shrinks to 0.925. That risks breaking the hand-to-lifter contact that binds the two figures together, even though no obvious tearing or ghosting is visible in the contact sheet.
The final full view is a good dwell image, but the opening frame is compromised by the barbell clipping and tight cropping of the lights/platform context.
fixes: move damped to 75% (cut-1 12% off-frame at t=0.00; cut-2 15% off-frame at t=0.00)

plan.rationale: A loss: the camera starts tight on the official bending over the fallen lifter and pulls back to zoom 1, the official shrinking as the dropped barbell, empty platform and silent crowd are revealed around the blackout.

rounds.verdict: rework: the plate has no visible defects (no stray text, no unwanted face detail, no anachronism or mangled anatomy), but the film is not publishable as submitted; the revised plan keeps the same layers and light-sweep while making the loss-reveal bolder and locking the official to the fallen lifter.
filmIssues: The pull-back idea is right for loss, but the executed move is only a modest 1.32 to 1.0 widening and reads close to a plain centred zoom-out in the contact sheet.

The t=0 frame is an awkward opening picture: the barbell is pressed against/clipped at the left edge, the hall and overhead lights are cropped, and the composition is neither a clean tight detail nor the full scene.

The official is a separate layer while the fallen lifter and platform remain in the background. With the official at high depth and slightly scaled down, his hand and feet drift subtly against the lifter/platform during the move, weakening the contact that is the emotional centre of the scene.
The light-sweep is not legible as a purposeful change in the still frames and does not compensate for the timid camera move.
